scenes.tts: How can a record full of gaps still show that life changed? A fossil scallop rests inside a Virginia riverbank. Above it, a modern river crosses land that was once beneath a shallow sea.
scenes.caption: How can a record full of gaps still show that life changed? A fossil scallop rests inside a Virginia riverbank. Above it, a modern river crosses land that was once beneath a shallow sea.
scenes.visual: Build the carried world for the whole film in sixteen-by-nine. COLOUR MAP, reused in the second film: fossils GOLD; matching body structures BLUE; DNA and protein sequences TEAL; supported inferences GREEN; missing or uncertain evidence GRAY. Keep labels at size twenty-eight or larger inside the safe frame, with at most six main objects visible. A large cutaway riverbank fills at least sixty percent of the frame height. A river moves slowly across the top. Below, broad sediment layers slide past as the camera moves downward. A GOLD fossil scallop appears inside one layer. A small label reads 'Virginia riverbank, schematic'. On the question, several GRAY gaps interrupt the layer stack without hiding the fossil.
scenes.narration: How can a record full of gaps still show that life changed? A fossil scallop rests inside a Virginia riverbank. Above it, a modern river crosses land that was once beneath a shallow sea.

scenes.visual: Title 'What the Rocks Still Show' fades in above the moving riverbank for two seconds. Water keeps flowing, tiny grains drift through the exposed bank, and the gold fossil remains visible.

scenes.tts: A fossil is the preserved remains or traces of past life. Shells, bones, teeth, and footprints can become fossils. Most remains rot or are eaten. Hard parts and quick burial improve the chance. The chance stays small.
scenes.caption: A fossil is the preserved remains or traces of past life. Shells, bones, teeth, and footprints can become fossils. Most remains rot or are eaten. Hard parts and quick burial improve the chance. The chance stays small.
scenes.visual: Move into the shallow sea that formed the lowest layer. A living scallop shell, a bone, a tooth, and a footprint appear one at a time as large simple GOLD silhouettes. Soft gray remains fade away or are carried off by scavenger icons. Sand sweeps over the shell quickly. The buried shell settles and the surrounding sand compresses into a rock layer. Keep 'schematic' on screen.
scenes.narration: A fossil is the preserved remains or traces of past life. Shells, bones, teeth, and footprints can become fossils. Most remains rot or are eaten. Hard parts and quick burial improve the chance. The chance stays small.

scenes.tts: All fossils found so far make the fossil record. Because fossilization is rare, that record has gaps. A gap means some details are missing. It does not make the fossils beside it disappear. The pattern can survive.
scenes.caption: All fossils found so far make the fossil record. Because fossilization is rare, that record has gaps. A gap means some details are missing. It does not make the fossils beside it disappear. The pattern can survive.
scenes.visual: The compressed layer joins a tall stack labelled 'fossil record'. Additional GOLD fossil silhouettes settle into several layers. Some intervals remain blank GRAY bands labelled 'gap'. On 'does not make', the gray bands widen slightly while the observed gold fossils on both sides stay bright and fixed. The river continues eroding the right edge, exposing more of the stack.
scenes.narration: All fossils found so far make the fossil record. Because fossilization is rare, that record has gaps. A gap means some details are missing. It does not make the fossils beside it disappear. The pattern can survive.

scenes.tts: In undisturbed layers, read from older below to younger above. Some kinds appear only in older rock. Some continue in changed forms. Sea shells inside inland rock also record an environment that is gone. Together, changes build history.
scenes.caption: In undisturbed layers, read from older below to younger above. Some kinds appear only in older rock. Some continue in changed forms. Sea shells inside inland rock also record an environment that is gone. Together, changes build history.
scenes.visual: A large arrow grows up the bank, labelled 'older' at the bottom and 'younger' at the top. A separate inset labelled 'older rock, western Virginia' shows one GOLD trilobite silhouette in its lower layers but not its upper ones; keep it apart from the riverbank stack. A sequence of scallop silhouettes changes slightly across higher layers without transforming one animal into another. The sea surface drains away and becomes the modern river landscape while shell fossils remain in the inland bank.
scenes.narration: In undisturbed layers, read from older below to younger above. Some kinds appear only in older rock. Some continue in changed forms. Sea shells inside inland rock also record an environment that is gone. Together, changes build history.

scenes.tts: Now remove one band of rock between two fossil layers. The lower layer holds one form. The upper layer holds a changed form. Does the missing band erase the pattern we can observe? Think before you decide.
scenes.caption: Now remove one band of rock between two fossil layers. The lower layer holds one form. The upper layer holds a changed form. Does the missing band erase the pattern we can observe? Think before you decide.
scenes.visual: Center two large rock layers. The lower layer contains one GOLD shell silhouette; the upper holds a related but changed GOLD shell silhouette. The band between them slides out and becomes a wide GRAY space marked 'missing layer'. White question text appears: 'Does a gap erase the observed pattern?' The river and loose grains slow to near-stillness.
scenes.narration: Now remove one band of rock between two fossil layers. The lower layer holds one form. The upper layer holds a changed form. Does the missing band erase the pattern we can observe? Think before you decide.

scenes.visual: Deliberate prediction pause. Keep the question and both observed fossils large. Only a faint shimmer crosses the gray missing band and a few grains drift from the bank.

scenes.tts: No. We can still compare the fossils on both sides. The gap limits what we know between them, so keep it gray. Evidence stays honest when the picture shows both observations and uncertainty. Limits stay visible.
scenes.caption: No. We can still compare the fossils on both sides. The gap limits what we know between them, so keep it gray. Evidence stays honest when the picture shows both observations and uncertainty. Limits stay visible.
scenes.visual: The question fades. A GREEN comparison bracket links the two observed GOLD fossils but stops at the GRAY band. The missing interval stays empty; no invented organism appears. Labels 'observed' attach to each fossil and 'unknown details' settles inside the gap. The comparison bracket gently pulses while erosion continues at the far edge.
scenes.narration: No. We can still compare the fossils on both sides. The gap limits what we know between them, so keep it gray. Evidence stays honest when the picture shows both observations and uncertainty. Limits stay visible.

scenes.tts: Different groups also appear at different places on a time strip. Fish, four-legged animals, mammal relatives, and bird-like dinosaurs have well-known early examples. They belong on separate branches, not one ladder. They are examples, not ancestors.
scenes.caption: Different groups also appear at different places on a time strip. Fish, four-legged animals, mammal relatives, and bird-like dinosaurs have well-known early examples. They belong on separate branches, not one ladder. They are examples, not ancestors.
scenes.visual: The layer stack rotates into a wide horizontal timeline. Put the lesson's four fossil examples at their table positions with numbers shown on screen but never spoken. Each GOLD example rises on its own short vertical branch from the timeline. A tempting single staircase appears in GRAY, receives a cross, and transforms into separate branching stems. Label the whole diagram 'examples, schematic branches'.
scenes.narration: Different groups also appear at different places on a time strip. Fish, four-legged animals, mammal relatives, and bird-like dinosaurs have well-known early examples. They belong on separate branches, not one ladder. They are examples, not ancestors.

scenes.tts: Fossils record existence, extinction, change, and past environments. Each observation supports some claims and not others. A shell can place life in an old sea. It cannot name every branch by itself. Evidence needs clear scope.
scenes.caption: Fossils record existence, extinction, change, and past environments. Each observation supports some claims and not others. A shell can place life in an old sea. It cannot name every branch by itself. Evidence needs clear scope.
scenes.visual: Return the timeline to the riverbank. Four large GREEN labels orbit the GOLD fossil record: 'existence', 'extinction', 'change', and 'environment'. As each label is named, one relevant fossil or layer brightens. On the limit, the orbit collapses back to the single scallop and a GRAY branching tree appears beside it with question marks, remaining unresolved.
scenes.narration: Fossils record existence, extinction, change, and past environments. Each observation supports some claims and not others. A shell can place life in an old sea. It cannot name every branch by itself. Evidence needs clear scope.

scenes.tts: In science, a theory is a well-tested explanation backed by many lines of evidence. Evolution explains why populations change and share ancestors. It also makes predictions that new evidence can test. That makes it testable.
scenes.caption: In science, a theory is a well-tested explanation backed by many lines of evidence. Evolution explains why populations change and share ancestors. It also makes predictions that new evidence can test. That makes it testable.
scenes.visual: The scallop layer, extinct trilobite, changing forms, and past-sea view slide into four large panels around a central GREEN block labelled 'evolution: tested explanation'. Thin green lines connect observations to the block. A new blank panel enters from the right labelled 'new evidence' and the central block sends a question-mark arrow toward it. Nothing is stamped proven or certain.
scenes.narration: In science, a theory is a well-tested explanation backed by many lines of evidence. Evolution explains why populations change and share ancestors. It also makes predictions that new evidence can test. That makes it testable.

scenes.tts: Return to the Virginia scallop. Its layer records a living thing and an ancient sea. Its resemblance to living scallops invites another question: which organisms share branches? Bones and sequences can test that next. The question continues.
scenes.caption: Return to the Virginia scallop. Its layer records a living thing and an ancient sea. Its resemblance to living scallops invites another question: which organisms share branches? Bones and sequences can test that next. The question continues.
scenes.visual: Zoom back to the original GOLD fossil scallop. Above it, a modern scallop silhouette drifts through shallow water. The old sea then morphs back into the modern river. At the right, unresolved GRAY branches grow. A BLUE bone-block icon and a TEAL sequence-strip icon move toward those branches but stop before attaching, preparing the second film without answering its question.
scenes.narration: Return to the Virginia scallop. Its layer records a living thing and an ancient sea. Its resemblance to living scallops invites another question: which organisms share branches? Bones and sequences can test that next. The question continues.

scenes.tts: The record is incomplete, so every claim keeps its limits. Still, observed fossils remain evidence. Across many layers, they show that life and environments changed through time.
scenes.caption: The record is incomplete, so every claim keeps its limits. Still, observed fossils remain evidence. Across many layers, they show that life and environments changed through time.
scenes.visual: Pull out to the full riverbank. GRAY gaps remain visible among many layers. GOLD fossils glow across the stack while the landscape above shifts slowly from shallow sea to river. A GREEN outline grows around the observed layers and fossils while leaving the gaps outside. The final thought settles as the scene dims.
scenes.narration: The record is incomplete, so every claim keeps its limits. Still, observed fossils remain evidence. Across many layers, they show that life and environments changed through time.

scenes.visual: One-line end card over the dimmed, still-moving riverbank. Large centered white text: 'Fossils reveal life's change through time, even with gaps.' No smaller line. Water and a few grains continue moving behind it.
